The soon-to-be 76-year-old had gone to the then-81-year-old Joe Biden in the summer of 2024 to say it was time to go. I come to you with a Tiny Question: What is the soul? Or, to be more personable: What is the soul for you? This is the question that dogged medieval mystics and murders and exiles and excommunications. One group thought one thing; another group thought another. It wasn’t all esoteric nonsense, of course: at the heart of it was the question whether illumination could be reached through reason, or whether it always came from outwith. recent_candidates.title: COP31 collapse highlights Africa's climate finance woes
recent_candidates.author: Jeronimo Gonzalez
recent_candidates.excerpt: The deep divisions between nations over climate finance, which contributed to the breakdown of COP31 talks, underscored the funding challenges facing African countries as they try to adapt to a warming planet. Although the continent contributes only 4% of global emissions , nine of the 10 most climate-vulnerable countries are in Africa , according to one study. In 2022, the continent received far less than the $190 billion required annually in climate funding, and its biggest economy alone needs more than $15 billion to fully implement climate adaptation policies over the next decade. While South Africa is experiencing heat waves that are damaging agricultural output, its grid remains heavily reliant on the sorts of fossil fuels that contribute the most to global emissions. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

Hakan Fidan made the remarks in a televised interview with Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday, saying Ankara had raised the possibility with regional allies, as well as US and European officials. recent_candidates.excerpt: The Latin American (LATAM) and Caribbean Basin have been significantly stigmatized as a drug-trafficking region that harbors Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCOs). Nations in this region, including Belize, have been combating TCOs with varying degrees of success. These successes are measured by seizure statisticsand by the street value of confiscated drugs. Each year, various US-based publications provide a statistical x-ray (cross-section) of what each of these nations is doing to prevent primarily cocaine from entering the US. Based on these metrics, the country may be blacklisted and, to a degree, reprimanded for not doing enough tocontribute to the unified action of stopping the flow of drugs. The focus should not be primarily on supply-side interdiction and tactical enforcement, but on a more balanced approach that targets the state’s core vulnerabilities: corruption, systemic judicial impunity, and the socio-economic drivers of criminal recruitment. The current strategy used by countries and partners in the region to combat TCOs is ineffective, as a focus on supply-side interdiction and tactical enforcement has historically failed. That same day, Russia launched a barrage of strikes on Ukraine, with two missiles and a jet-powered drone landing in Poland. recent_candidates.title: Why Europe is bunkering down
recent_candidates.author: Juliette Bretan
recent_candidates.excerpt: There’s a secret beneath Helsinki. Dig 25 meters down beneath its granite crust, and you’ll find vast hockey pitches, brightly colored swimming pools, adventure playgrounds and the city’s first-ever axe-throwing venue. It’s called HELAXE, and notes on its website that “bowling is for pussies!”. Yet in a matter of hours, these spaces, one the size of a seven-story building, can be utterly transformed: the pitches removed and the pool water drained to be replaced with decontamination showers and enough bunk beds for 6,000 people. With the Russian frontier just 100 miles away, and Putin’s gray-zone operations ramping up, these are bunkers fit for an age of uncertainty. Helsinki has offered inspiration to a vast array of European leaders and delegations, each seeking to fashion their own approaches to shelters and civil defense. Across Europe, nations, cities, and even private citizens are reimagining subterranean space as we are told to prepare for a “Black Sky” event . It all reflects a distinct shift in the conception of conflict among its citizens. Where, in the past, wars might have seemed like something that happened in far-off fields, the rise in these dual-use bunkers, blending the mundane with the martial, suggests preparedness is increasingly becoming just another part of life. recent_candidates.title: Bulgari, adiós a la ‘dolce vita’
recent_candidates.author: Javier Rioyo
recent_candidates.excerpt: Nunca vi sudar a Paolo Bulgari . Ya estuviéramos cerca del desierto, navegando por el Mediterráneo, en su riad palaciego de Marrakech, en una terraza romana, en Nápoles en ferragosto, en los veranos de Madrid o en una cala de Ibiza. Lo conocí una noche romana de mediados de los años noventa. Ya era la pareja —todavía sin «oficializar» la relación— de una de mis más queridas amigas, una joven compañera de los tiempos de Cueto, del nacimiento del Canal+ , que se iniciaba en el oficio entre la radio —la SER—, el periodismo escrito — El País — y los nuevos lenguajes de una televisión de modelo francés y experimento español. Ni la nostalgia ni la melancolía sirven de nada y no lloraremos sobre la leche derramada; tuvimos y seguimos contando con la amistad de Maite Carpio , así que pase la vida. Maite, la mujer de Paolo, nuestra amiga, es y siempre será el amor de sus últimos, felices, treinta años y la madre de dos adoradas hijas. Maite y Paolo tuvieron un flechazo, uno de esos encuentros capaces de unir pasión, amor, cercanía, convivencia y complicidad, sin que eso quiera decir que vivieran en una balsa de aceite. Su viaje tuvo mareas, peligros y cantos de sirena, sin dejar de compartir rumbo, cariño y una admiración en dos sentidos. Dos que supieron navegar juntos hasta el final. El sábado 21 de noviembre murió en su eterna Roma el más refinado de los joyeros, el condottiere de Via Condotti. recent_candidates.title: Hallan restos de las explosiones volcánicas submarinas más profundas conocidas
recent_candidates.author: Sinc
recent_candidates.excerpt: Un equipo internacional liderado por la Universidad de Texas en Dallas (EE UU) ha encontrado rocas de erupciones volcánicas explosivas a más de 6 000 metros de profundidad, junto al Challenger Deep, el punto más hondo del océano. Son las más profundas de este tipo que se conocen, según publican hoy en la revista Frontiers in Earth Science . Los investigadores las localizaron con el robot submarino Jason en una campaña a finales de 2024, en la fosa de las Marianas (Pacífico occidental). Se trata de flujos piroclásticos : fragmentos de magma que una erupción explosiva lanza y que, en este caso, se depositaron en capas sobre el fondo y se soldaron en roca dura cuando aún estaban calientes. Investigadores de la expedición clasifican en el laboratorio del barco las rocas recuperadas por el robot. / Clinton Crowley (UT Dallas) «Sabíamos que procedían de una erupción submarina profunda por la abundancia de fragmentos volcánicos rotos, el vidrio volcánico de la matriz y porque eran rocas bastante resistentes, lo que indica que conservaban calor suficiente para soldarse», explica a SINC Robert J. Stern , geólogo de la Universidad de Texas en Dallas y autor principal del estudio. recent_candidates.excerpt: El ministro de Exteriores de Irán , Abbas Araqchi, ha considerado que los planes de Estados Unidos para imponer algún tipo de bloqueo terrestre al país son simplemente absurdos por consideraciones geográficas y por las relaciones diplomáticas que preserva la República Islámica. Trump se «inclina» por reanudar los ataques contra Irán si no hay acuerdo para Año Nuevo THE OBJECTIVE Las provincias fronterizas, en particular, han desarrollado fuertes lazos entre los habitantes al otro lado de las aduanas, con los que comparten raíces históricas y culturales y «poseen la capacidad de abrir lo que el enemigo pretende cerrar» .
